request_text: We shot this sofa in our showroom but there's a staff member in the background on the left. Can you take him out? Everything else should stay exactly as it is — same sofa, same room, same light. We're using it on the product page tomorrow.

supplied_inputs.description: showroom photograph containing the sofa and an unintended person

hard: the sofa must be unchanged in shape, colour and position
room and lighting must remain the same
no person may appear in the result
free: how the vacated background area is filled

preservation_semantics: THE DEFINING PROPERTY OF THIS ITEM. One named element is removed; everything else is implicitly preserved. The customer enumerated nothing to keep, and the system must not manufacture a list of preserve statements and attribute them to the customer.
acceptance_relevant: the sofa is recognisably the same object
no visible artefact where the person was

request_text: इस पैक फोटो का background बदल कर सफेद कर दीजिए, e-commerce listing के लिए चाहिए. पैक पर जो लिखा है "शुद्ध मसाले" और "५०० ग्राम" वो बिल्कुल वैसा ही रहना चाहिए, एक भी अक्षर बदलना नहीं चाहिए. पैक का रंग भी वही रहे.

supplied_inputs.description: spice pack photographed against a cluttered background

hard: the Devanagari strings "शुद्ध मसाले" and "५०० ग्राम" must survive byte-exact

preservation_semantics: Text preservation under an edit is a DIFFERENT requirement from text generation. The characters already exist in the supplied image and must survive the operation intact — including the conjunct in "शुद्ध" and the Devanagari digits in "५००", which are exactly the characters most likely to be damaged or silently re-rendered when the surrounding area changes.
acceptance_relevant: both Devanagari strings render byte-exact and legible
language_dependency: Devanagari conjuncts and Devanagari digits are the hard case for text SURVIVAL under an edit, and the failure mode differs from Latin: a damaged matra produces a plausible-looking wrong word rather than obvious garbage. An English version of this item would not test the same thing.

request_text: Ye wala creative pichle month ka hai. Bas price change karna hai — "₹24,999" ki jagah "₹21,499" kar do, aur "Limited offer" ko "अभी खरीदें" se replace kar do. Baaki sab same rahe, layout, colours, product photo, sab kuch. Font bhi wahi rakhna.

supplied_inputs.description: finished promotional creative from a previous campaign

hard: layout, palette, product photograph and typeface unchanged

preservation_semantics: A targeted text substitution inside a finished creative. Two elements change; everything else is named as preserved by the customer, unusually — most edit requests leave preservation implicit. Recorded as customer_specified here BECAUSE THEY SAID IT, which is the distinction the provenance rule exists to protect.
acceptance_relevant: new price string exact, including the comma
the replaced line occupies the original position without disturbing layout
language_dependency: The substitution switches SCRIPT — a Latin/currency string and a Devanagari string in the same creative, replacing a Latin phrase with a Devanagari one. Script-switching inside an existing layout is a distinct requirement: the replacement has different metrics and must still fit.

request_text: This is a photo of our founder from 1961 for our anniversary campaign. It's got creases, a water stain across the bottom right, and the whole thing has faded. Can you clean it up? Please don't change his face or make him look younger — it should still look like a photograph from 1961, just an undamaged one.

supplied_inputs.description: damaged monochrome photograph, creased, stained and faded

intents.evidence_quote: don't change his face or make him look younger

hard: the result must still read as a 1961 photograph
soft: damage removal as complete as possible

preservation_semantics: WHY RESTORE IS NOT A KIND OF EDIT, made concrete. An edit is judged against the change requested. A restoration is judged against a plausible original THAT NOBODY HAS. The customer's real constraint is negative — do not invent detail, do not modernise — and that acceptance semantic has no equivalent in an edit request.
acceptance_relevant: period character retained; no invented detail

request_text: Take this packshot of our steel bottle and give me a six-second clip for the website hero. I want the camera to move slowly around it, nothing else. The bottle shouldn't move or change — same bottle, same label, same reflections behaving properly. No text, no music.

supplied_inputs.description: studio packshot of a brushed-steel bottle

intents.evidence_quote: The bottle shouldn't move or change

hard: the bottle does not move or deform
soft: reflections behave plausibly for a brushed metal surface

preservation_semantics: THE CAMERA/SUBJECT SEPARATION TEST, in its cleanest form. Camera motion is requested; subject motion is explicitly refused. A system that models "motion" as one property cannot express this request at all, and cannot diagnose the most likely failure — the object drifting or warping while the camera moves.
acceptance_relevant: no warping or identity drift across frames

request_text: इस फोटो को आठ सेकंड का वीडियो बना दीजिए. चाय की भाप ऊपर उठती दिखे और आदमी हल्का सा मुस्कुराए, बस इतना ही — कैमरा स्थिर रहे. आखिर में नीचे "स्वाद चाय" लिखा रहे, पूरे वीडियो में स्थिर और साफ़ पढ़ने लायक.

supplied_inputs.description: still photograph of a man holding a cup of tea

hard: "स्वाद चाय" remains stable and legible for the whole clip
facial identity consistent across all frames

preservation_semantics: The inverse of RX-05: subject motion requested, camera motion refused. Two different subject motion types in one item — object motion and micro-expression — which the grammar separates because they fail differently.
acceptance_relevant: Devanagari text stable and legible in every frame
face remains the same person across frames
language_dependency: Text STABILITY UNDER MOTION is a distinct requirement from static text rendering, and Devanagari is the hard case: a conjunct or matra that flickers between frames produces a different word frame-to-frame while each frame looks individually plausible. Latin text does not fail this way.

request_text: We have this landscape banner but we need a vertical version for Stories. Can you extend the image top and bottom so it works at 9:16? Don't crop the boat or the headline — they need to stay fully visible and in the same relationship to each other.

supplied_inputs.description: horizontal banner containing a boat and a headline

hard: spatial relationship between boat and headline preserved
soft: extended area consistent with the existing scene
free: what appears in the newly created area

preservation_semantics: Extend differs from edit in what is at risk: nothing existing should change, but new area must be invented, and the customer has constrained what must survive rather than what must appear. Note the customer asked to EXTEND, not to crop or reframe — a system that satisfied 9:16 by cropping would have substituted a different operation for the one requested.
acceptance_relevant: 9:16 achieved by extension, not by cropping

request_text: Do photos bhej raha hoon — ek model ka portrait hai, doosra hamare lipstick pack ka packshot. Dono ko ek creative mein combine karna hai, model haath mein product pakde hue dikhe. Model ka face bilkul same rehna chahiye aur pack ka shade bhi exactly same — wo hamara signature colour hai. Upar likha ho "नया शेड, वही भरोसा".

intents.evidence_quote: Model ka face bilkul same rehna chahiye
pack ka shade bhi exactly same

hard: model's face identical to the supplied portrait

preservation_semantics: TWO IDENTITY REFERENCES AT ONCE, from two separate supplied assets, with a NEW RELATIONSHIP that exists in neither. Note the asset role here is identity_reference and NOT subject_of_operation — neither supplied image is being modified; both inform a new artefact. That is the distinction RX-01 through RX-04 would get wrong if roles were assigned by "an asset was attached".
acceptance_relevant: the holding relationship is physically plausible
language_dependency: The headline is Devanagari while the request is Hinglish, which is the ordinary way this customer writes — and it separates the SPOKEN/instruction language from the ON-SCREEN COPY language, a distinction R10 exists to carry and which a single-language item cannot exercise.

request_text: Ek hi offer creative chahiye but chaar alag versions — Hindi, Tamil, Bengali aur English. Offer same hai, "Buy 1 Get 1" aur price "₹199". Visual bilkul identical rehna chahiye chaaron mein, sirf language badle. Hum chaaron use karenge, koi choose nahi karna.

hard: visual composition identical across all four
soft: copy reads naturally in each language

preservation_semantics: Preservation ACROSS a set rather than within one artefact. The invariant is the composition, and it must hold between deliverables — a requirement with no analogue in any single-output item.

deliverable_set.note: "koi choose nahi karna" — the customer will use all four, so every one must be acceptable. This is per_deliverable, NOT best_n_of_m, and the difference changes the cost of acceptance by a factor of four.

acceptance_relevant: each language rendered correctly, including three different scripts
price string exact in all four
language_dependency: LANGUAGE IS THE VARIATION AXIS ITSELF. The item spans three non-Latin scripts (Devanagari, Tamil, Bengali) plus Latin, and the requirement is that a fixed layout accommodate all four — different text metrics, different line-breaking, different glyph heights. This cannot be tested in one language by construction.

request_text: We're launching a new programme and need a small campaign set from one idea: one square static for the feed, one vertical static for Stories, and one six-second vertical video. Same concept, same colours, same headline across all three. Show us the set — we'll take it or leave it as a whole, we don't want to mix and match with something else.

hard: exactly three deliverables — 1:1 static, 9:16 static, 9:16 video ~6s
soft: video shares visual language with the statics
free: how the concept is adapted per format

preservation_semantics: A campaign set spanning MODALITIES — two statics and a video from one concept. Consistency must hold across media types, not just across crops.

deliverable_set.note: "take it or leave it as a whole" makes acceptance SET-LEVEL. One weak deliverable fails the set. This is the sharpest CpAO case in the bank: the cost of acceptance is not the sum of three independent acceptances.

acceptance_relevant: three deliverables in the stated formats
the set reads as one campaign

request_text: ROUND 1 — "Is cake photo ka background thoda brighten kar do." ROUND 2 — "Achha hua, but ab thoda zyada warm kar do." ROUND 3 — "Perfect. Ab isme "Fresh Daily" bhi add kar do upar."

free: placement of the added text beyond "upar"

preservation_semantics: THE REASON THIS ITEM IS NOT RUNNABLE. Round 2 says "thoda zyada warm" — MORE warm than what? Than the round-1 output, which is not the supplied asset. Round 3's "isme" refers to the round-2 result. Neither round is interpretable against the original input alone, and the project has no frozen contract for what a later round inherits from an earlier one.

deliverable_set.note: cardinality applies to the final deliverable; intermediate rounds are not deliverables

acceptance_relevant: NOT DEFINED. Acceptance semantics across rounds are exactly what is deferred.
language_dependency: Relative-degree revisions ("thoda zyada warm") are how this customer population actually issues follow-ups, and the referring expressions ("isme") carry the inheritance problem in a way a formal English rewrite would smooth away — which would hide the very thing the probe exists to expose.
